name: Spondyloepimetaphyseal Dysplasia, Strudwick Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for SEMD Strudwick Type

criteria.description: Short stature with disproportionate shortening of trunk and limbs
Platyspondyly and other vertebral anomalies on imaging
Irregular metaphyseal changes in long bones visible on radiographs
Identification of pathogenic COL2A1 gene mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major clinical and radiographic criteria; genetic testing supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiographic; genetic testing aids confirmation.

pathognomonic.notes: Flattened vertebral bodies characteristic on spinal imaging
Disproportionate short stature with trunk involvement

common.notes: Degenerative joint disease in adolescence or early adulthood
Waddling or limping gait due to skeletal deformities

occasional.notes: Increased risk due to collagen abnormalities
Restrictive lung disease secondary to thoracic deformities
Exaggerated inward curvature of the lumbar spine

rare.notes: Potential for cervical spinal cord compression
Due to spinal cord compression or instability

imaging: Metaphyseal irregularities and flaring on long bone radiographs
Coxa vara deformity on hip imaging
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in COL2A1 gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Clinical assessment of disproportionate short stature
Family history may be positive for autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: More severe vertebral and epiphyseal involvement
Earlier and more pronounced skeletal deformities
Short-limbed dwarfism with normal trunk length
Characteristic radiographic features distinct from SEMD

redFlags: Progressive neurological symptoms indicating spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic deformity
Rapid progression of skeletal deformities causing functional impairment
references: Spranger JW, et al. Bone Dysplasias: An Atlas of Genetic Disorders of Skeletal Development. 2002.
Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2019 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
